name: barmark
shortDescription: Our open-source plain-text notation for chord charts: the bar grid musicians already write, specified precisely enough for machines to parse and render.
description: barmark is a Markdown-inspired notation for chord charts. It takes the bar-grid convention musicians already write in plain text ("| D | A | Bm | G |") and specifies it precisely: what an empty cell means, how far "x 2" reaches, how repeats, sections, key, meter and tempo are written. A barmark file is a markdown file (.chart.md), so it reads well anywhere markdown does.

It ships as two packages. barmark itself is the parser, canonical printer and Harte-label converter, with no runtime dependencies. @barmark/render renders a chart as an accessible, evenly spaced bar grid, as static HTML or as a web component. We extracted it from Stem Shovel's chart parser and validated its rules in our stem-bench research. The code is MIT licensed; the grammar is a v0.1 draft.

relatedArticle.title: Barmark: Chord Charts Bands and Machines Can Both Read

useCases: Writing chord charts in plain text that software can read without guessing
Parsing charts into bars, sections and chords for playback, alignment or analysis
Rendering clean, accessible chord-chart grids on web pages with or without JavaScript
